open_obligations.what_is_open: A finite real semialgebraic atlas on every intersection in the complement of the six principal cubic charts, together with the exceptional real fibers of the exact fixed published full second-and-third-moment map.
open_obligations.obstruction: The proved product and sign chart does not determine real primary components when several factors vanish. Alternate adjugate columns can remove some failures, whereas a full-moment ambiguity requires covariance-compatible twins; neither follows from denominator vanishing alone.
open_obligations.attempted: The principal arbitrary-real chart was solved exactly. A removable fixed-order zero-column boundary and a genuine cubic zero-skew coefficient fiber were also derived, but they do not enumerate all intersections or settle covariance compatibility.

prose_updates.tldr: A principal semialgebraic chart for each of the six labeled chains identifies the order and both coefficients from the cubic tensor over arbitrary real parameters whenever the exact product, sign, and terminal-slice conditions hold. The cubic image of the positive-skew bounded model is a strict compact subclass of this chart and supplies uniform determinant and denominator margins, honest bounded-moment inversion, and a constant-cost implementation. The exact fixed published one-proxy graph is treated separately by an analytic parameterization and ideal-membership argument, not by a claimed execution or archival reproduction of the released basis. Complete real-fiber classification on the exceptional complement remains open, with one removable zero-column failure and one genuine cubic zero-skew ambiguity already certified.

project_justification.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025) report third-order nonidentification on a fixed graph with unrestricted real coefficients. That setting is not the same as the unknown-order positive-skew class, and generic elimination does not distinguish removable rational-chart failures from genuine real ambiguity on exceptional intersections.
project_justification.niche: The joint three-variable cubic tensor has a principal rank-sign geometry: one rank-two slice selects the root, its kernel sign cell selects the middle, and adjugate contractions recover both edges. This geometry extends beyond the compact box to an explicit semialgebraic chart over arbitrary real parameters.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the principal real cubic inverse, derives the positive-box margins as a quantitative corollary, keeps the fixed published ideal analysis separate and analytic, proves covariance-only overlap, attaches honest finite-sample inversion, and isolates the full exceptional real-fiber atlas as the remaining problem.

prose_updates.related_work: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorems 3.5--3.6, Figure 3, Appendix C.1.1, and the released Macaulay2 file specify the exact fixed one-proxy graph and its reported higher-order boundary. This note does not claim to have rerun or archived a reduction against the released stored basis. Its fixed-graph component instead derives the displayed relation analytically from the exact parameterized moment map and applies ideal and localization consequences at the level proved in the formal statements. The six-order principal chart is a different result: it concerns an explicit sign-and-nonvanishing domain and therefore does not identify the unrestricted published class. Cai et al. (2023) motivate closed-form cumulant extraction for one latent component but combine covariance with a selected higher order. Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024) motivate source-rank diagnostics using stacked orders. Garcia-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010) provide the elimination-ideal framework, while Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (2011) motivate the distinction between generic and global fibers. Ghassami et al. (2020) motivate comparison of whole model images. Babii (2020) and Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) inform inversion-based confidence sets, but not this finite union of exact cubic charts.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: No executed independent replication, pinned stored-basis normal-form output, or archived Macaulay2 receipt is claimed. The fixed published component rests on analytic membership derived from the parameterization and kernel contraction; zero normal form against any genuine Groebner basis is a mathematical consequence of membership, not evidence that a particular released command was run. The principal chart is sufficient but not exhaustive. Its complement contains both removable coordinate failures and genuine cubic ambiguities, and the complete real primary decomposition of all rank, sign, and denominator intersections is not supplied. A cubic twin is not promoted to a full second-and-third-moment twin without matching covariance.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The widest proved unknown-order result is the principal real cubic chart defined by the exact product, two sign inequalities, and nonzero terminal-slice determinant. The cubic image \(\{C_3(P):P\in\mathcal P_+\}\) of the compact law class lies inside that chart and is used for uniform numerical margins and finite-sample coverage. Neither theorem identifies the unrestricted fixed published class merely by subclass inclusion. The separate published-map statements are analytic ideal consequences only, with no claim of an independently executed basis replication. Outside the principal chart, only the explicitly proved removable boundary and cubic ambiguity are classified; the full exceptional atlas remains open. On the fixed order \(1\to2\to3\), the recovered terminal edge is the same structural coordinate used by the published fourth-order target, which is target compatibility rather than unrestricted-class identification.
